column1: # Required-check wall-clock latency bounds for watch-wallclock-p90-11774.sh
#   check_name   the required check-run name — MUST match a non-comment row of
#                required context with no row here is itself a ratchet finding)
#   pr_bound_s   bound in SECONDS on pull_request-surface latency
#   mq_bound_s   bound in SECONDS on merge_group-surface latency
#   margin_frac  drift margin — breach iff measured p90 > bound * (1 + margin)
# latency_s = check.completed_at - sampled ci.yml run.created_at (queue wait +
# runner acquisition + every serialized predecessor + execution — the wall clock
# a PR or merge-queue entry actually experiences; see the "Runner-availability
# data" cohort model in the sharding runbook).
# SEEDING METHOD (2026-11-02 baseline): bound = the measured p90 latency of the
# last ~30 completed+conclusion=success ci.yml runs per surface, rounded UP to
# the next minute; margin 0.30 (the shard-balance-watch LEG_DRIFT_RATIO
# precedent). Bounds are seeded from the MEASURED baseline, not the epic target
# (PR p90 <= 1200 s / merge-queue p90 <= 900 s) — seeding at target would have
# fired immediately: `test` measured p90 3036 s (PR) / 2798 s (merge queue).
# The epic goal is reported as a separate column in the tracker body. Tighten a
# bound only after the measured p90 has held below the new value; a bound may
# loosen only with the measurement recorded in the runbook.
# Blank lines and #-comments are ignored. A row with an unparsable number or a
# wrong column count is a cannot-establish error in the probe, never a silent
